title: D1-1c | Existing Pump Reuse and Cleaning Trigger
question_prompt:
D1-1c | Existing Pump Reuse and Cleaning Trigger

An expansion project proposes to reuse an existing pump with a maximum continuous discharge pressure of 65.0 bar. Membrane A-value and channel pressure drop differ among clean, aged, and fouled states. Determine the minimum pressure meeting all constraints in each state, decide whether the pump can be reused, and define a cleaning trigger. Site policy requires cleaning when the modeled pressure requirement reaches 64.50 bar, leaving only 0.50 bar reserve to the continuous limit.

Fixed parameter | Value | Unit | Status | Membrane state | A_comp (m/s/Pa) | Pressure drop (bar)
Feed mass flow | 3.9 | kg/s | Fixed / locked | A Clean | 4.2e-12 | 0.8
Membrane area | 390 | m^2 | Fixed / locked | B Aged | 3.5e-12 | 1.5
Feed NaCl | 0.036 | mass fraction | Fixed / locked | C Fouled | 3e-12 | 2.6
Temperature | 20 | deg C | Fixed / locked
B_comp | 3.5e-08 | m/s | Fixed / locked | Acceptance constraints
Permeate pressure | 1.013 | bar | Fixed / locked | Permeate production, Qp | >= 6.70 m^3/h | Each condition
Channel height | 0.002 | m | Fixed / locked | Water recovery | <= 55.0% | Each condition
Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Fixed / locked | Average water flux | <= 21.0 LMH | Each condition
Module length | 20 | m | Fixed / locked | Salt rejection | >= 98.75% | Each condition
Permeate NaCl | <= 450 mg/L | Each condition

Required work
1. Treat this as a multi-condition pressure-sizing and feasibility problem. Do not change locked membrane or hydraulic parameters while searching pressure.
4. Compare all Pmin values or infeasibility evidence with the stated equipment margin, limits, or control window, then make the engineering decision.
5. Distinguish equipment rating/limits from operating setpoints. Do not hide a membrane-flux or water-quality violation by blindly increasing pressure.

Required pressure resolution: 0.05 bar. Any design margin, pump limit, VFD lower limit, maintenance reserve, or equipment selection increment in this benchmark is a stated rule used to produce a unique, auditable answer.

The existing pump covers the clean and aged states, but the fouled-state Pmin is 66.80 bar, which exceeds the 65.0 bar continuous limit by 1.80 bar. Under the stated reserve policy, cleaning is triggered when the modeled Pmin reaches 64.50 bar; the aged state is still operable, while continued degradation toward the fouled state is not acceptable.

Simulator evidence note: The fouled-state boundary was simulator-verified at 66.75 bar fail and 66.80 bar pass.
